dedupe_keys.name: multi hazard disaster impact outputs from synthetic future urban scenarios in 10 cities tomorrow s cities

description: This dataset gives spatially explicit disaster risk outputs for future urban development scenarios drawn up by community groups in 10 study areas: Istanbul, Nablus, Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Nairobi, Nakuru, Quito, Kokhana and Rapti in Nepal, and Darussalam in Tanzania. It is published by the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology's Environmental Information Data Centre (9 April 2026), with authors from University College London, An-Najah National University, the GEM Foundation, People in Need, Nepal's National Society for Earthquake Technology, Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology, Lund University and others, as case studies for the Tomorrow's Cities 'Tomorrowville' virtual testbed, funded by NERC through the GCRF Urban Disaster Risk Hub. It quantifies physical, social and economic risk from earthquakes, floods or landslides interacting with planned land use and building types: damage states for each building and eight social metrics, including unemployed workers, children without education access, households and people without hospital access, displacement, homelessness and casualties. Coverage: the 10 study areas. Access: EIDC download and a supporting ZIP with a readme on how each metric is computed. Licence: Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: synthetic future scenarios. Simulation uses: risk-informed urban planning and testing land-use choices. Related records: the Tomorrowville virtual urban testbed.
